paragraphs: Calix sells to broadband service providers, describing itself as an AI platform company that enables them to transform their operations. Its SmartLife line is pitched at providers that want to give a community what it needs to connect and thrive in the places people live, work, learn, and play.

For utilities, the company presents fiber optics as a high-speed communication backbone that modernizes grid operations. Low latency fiber, it says, lets fault location, isolation and service restoration systems pinpoint outages and reroute power in seconds. Passive optical network architecture connects multiple grid endpoints using a single fiber line, which the company frames as lower equipment and cabling expense. Related access hardware brings 100G, high-density OLT, aggregation, and subscriber management together in one appliance.

The grid pages address electric utilities alongside broadband companies in underserved communities that share infrastructure in rural areas. Calix promotes a customer conference, ConneXions, on its home page. A company announcement names a new chief marketing officer as Calix extends the value of its AI-native platform for service providers and adjacent markets.

quote.text: Calix is an AI platform company that enables service providers to transform their operations
